On July 11, 2014, LeBron James announced on *[Sports Illustrated](/wiki/Sports_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")* 's website that after opting out of the final year of his contract, he would leave the Heat and return to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers").[[27]](#cite_note-27) Wade and Bosh stayed in Miami. Like the Cavaliers in the 2010 off-season, the Heat focused on how it would maintain itself without LeBron. Wade and Bosh were joined by returning players [Mario Chalmers](/wiki/Mario_Chalmers "Mario Chalmers"), [Norris Cole](/wiki/Norris_Cole_(basketball) "Norris Cole (basketball)"), [Udonis Haslem](/wiki/Udonis_Haslem "Udonis Haslem") and [Chris Andersen](/wiki/Chris_Andersen "Chris Andersen") along with former rivals [Luol Deng](/wiki/Luol_Deng "Luol Deng") and [Danny Granger](/wiki/Danny_Granger "Danny Granger"). The Heat also drafted [Shabazz Napier](/wiki/Shabazz_Napier "Shabazz Napier") and [James Ennis](/wiki/James_Ennis_(basketball) "James Ennis (basketball)"). In 2015, they also gained [Goran Dragić](/wiki/Goran_Dragi%C4%87 "Goran Dragić") and his younger brother [Zoran Dragić](/wiki/Zoran_Dragi%C4%87 "Zoran Dragić").

After a season with several injuries, including to Chris Bosh and Josh McRoberts, the Heat finished with a 37–45 record, the NBA's 10th-worst. They failed to make the playoffs after being Eastern Conference champions four straight years. It was the second time in Wade's career they did not qualify for the postseason. The Heat were the first team since the [2004–05 Los Angeles Lakers](/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "2004–05 Los Angeles Lakers season") to miss the playoffs after going to the NBA Finals the previous year. Miami had qualified for the playoffs for six consecutive seasons.

Main articles: [Croatian language](/wiki/Croatian_language "Croatian language"), [Languages of Croatia](/wiki/Languages_of_Croatia "Languages of Croatia"), [Minority languages of Croatia](/wiki/Minority_languages_of_Croatia "Minority languages of Croatia"), and [Bunjevac dialect](/wiki/Bunjevac_dialect "Bunjevac dialect")

See also: [Shtokavian dialect](/wiki/Shtokavian_dialect "Shtokavian dialect"), [Chakavian dialect](/wiki/Chakavian_dialect "Chakavian dialect"), and [Kajkavian dialect](/wiki/Kajkavian_dialect "Kajkavian dialect")

Croatian is the official language of the Republic of Croatia and has been an [official language of the European Union](/wiki/Official_languages_of_the_European_Union "Official languages of the European Union") since Croatia's accession in 2013.[[293]](#cite_note-Ustav-RH-296)[[294]](#cite_note-VL-Hrvatski-EU-297) Croatian replaced [Latin](/wiki/Latin "Latin") as the official language of the Croatian government in the 19th century.[[295]](#cite_note-Iadertina-Hr-298) Following the [Vienna Literary Agreement](/wiki/Vienna_Literary_Agreement "Vienna Literary Agreement") in 1850, the language and its Latin alphabet underwent reforms to create an unified "Croatian or Serbian" or "[Serbo-Croatian](/wiki/Serbo-Croatian "Serbo-Croatian")" standard, which under various names became the official language of [Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia").[[296]](#cite_note-299) In [SFR Yugoslavia](/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia"), from 1972 to 1989, the language was constitutionally designated as the "Croatian literary language" and the "Croatian or Serbian language". It was the result of a resistance to and [secession](/wiki/Language_secessionism "Language secessionism") from "Serbo-Croatian" in the form of the [Declaration on the Status and Name of the Croatian Literary Language](/wiki/Declaration_on_the_Status_and_Name_of_the_Croatian_Liter

Shelley Moore Capito :: Early life and education :: chunk_0002
Shelley Wellons Moore Capito was born in [Glen Dale, West Virginia](/wiki/Glen_Dale,_West_Virginia "Glen Dale, West Virginia"), on November 26, 1953. She is the daughter of [Shelley](/wiki/Shelley_Riley_Moore "Shelley Riley Moore") (née Riley) and [Arch Alfred Moore Jr.](/wiki/Arch_A._Moore_Jr. "Arch A. Moore Jr."),[[1]](#cite_note-1) who served three terms as the state's [governor](/wiki/List_of_governors_of_West_Virginia "List of governors of West Virginia"). A resident of Charleston, Capito was educated at the [Holton-Arms School](/wiki/Holton-Arms_School "Holton-Arms School"), a private college-preparatory school in [Bethesda, Maryland](/wiki/Bethesda,_Maryland "Bethesda, Maryland");[[2]](#cite_note-2) [Duke University](/wiki/Duke_University "Duke University"), where she earned her bachelor's degree in [zoology](/wiki/Zoology "Zoology"); and the [University of Virginia School of Education and Human Development](/wiki/University_of_Virginia_School_of_Education_and_Human_Development "University of Virginia School of Education and Human Development"), where she earned her master's degree.[[3]](#cite_note-3) She is a member of [Kappa Kappa Gamma](/wiki/Kappa_Kappa_Gamma "Kappa Kappa Gamma") sorority[[4]](#cite_note-4) and represented West Virginia as the 1972 [Cherry Blossom Princess](/wiki/National_Cherry_Blossom_Festival "National Cherry Blossom Festival").[[5]](#cite_note-5)

After earning her master's degree, Capito was a career counselor at [West Virginia State University](/wiki/West_Virginia_State_University "West Virginia State University") and director of the educational information center for the West Virginia Board of Regents.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

Capito was elected to Kanawha County's seat in the [state House of Delegates](/wiki/West_Virginia_House_of_Delegates "West Virginia House of Delegates") in 1996, and served two terms, from 1996 to 2000.[[7]](#cite_note-:6-7)

Tacko Fall :: Early life :: chunk_0001
Fall was born and raised in [Dakar](/wiki/Dakar "Dakar"), Senegal. In 2011, Senegalese basketball coach Ibrahima N'Diaye, the brother of former NBA player [Mamadou N'Diaye](/wiki/Mamadou_N%27Diaye_(basketball,_born_1975) "Mamadou N'Diaye (basketball, born 1975)"), heard from a friend about an exceptionally tall teenager that he had seen playing with friends in a local street.[[8]](#cite_note-Forbes1-8) After identifying him, they visited the 15-year-old Fall—who already stood 7 ft 3 in (2.21 m) tall—at his home and persuaded Fall's mother, Marianne Diop Sene, to allow Fall to start attending N'Diaye's basketball academy.[[8]](#cite_note-Forbes1-8) Fall moved to the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") at age 16. He first played organized basketball in [Houston](/wiki/Houston "Houston"), Texas, and trained with [NBA Hall-of-Famer](/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame") [Hakeem Olajuwon](/wiki/Hakeem_Olajuwon "Hakeem Olajuwon").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

Fall was listed as 7 ft 6 in (2.29 m) and was purportedly still growing around his senior year, making him the tallest high-school basketball player in the country while he played for [Jamie's House Charter](/wiki/Jamie%27s_House_Charter_School "Jamie's House Charter School") and [Liberty Christian Prep](/wiki/Liberty_Christian_Preparatory_School "Liberty Christian Preparatory School").[[10]](#cite_note-orlandosentinel-10)

Due to his height and reach, Fall was one of the most highly scouted high-school basketball centers in the nation. He first played for [Jamie's House Charter School](/wiki/Jamie%27s_House_Charter_School "Jamie's House Charter School") in Houston, where his team won the state championship. Fall played with ISTI all-stars summer travel team and for Each 1 Teach 1 on the [Nike Elite Youth Basketball League](/wiki/Nike_Elite_Youth_Basketball_League "Nike Elite Youth Basketball League") (EYBL) circuit

2. Most individual swimming Olympic gold medals
3. Most medals won at the FINA Swimming World Championships
4. Most Olympic gold medals in team swimming
5. Most medals won at the Olympics for swimming (male)
6. Most Men's World Swimmer of the Year Awards
7. Most Olympic golds at one Games (male)
8. Most gold medals won at the Olympics for an individual event (male)
9. Most FINA world records held by an individual
10. Most Olympic medals won, Men
11. Most consecutive Olympic swimming gold medals in the same event (male)
12. Fastest swim long course 400 metres medley (male)
13. Most gold medals won at the Olympics (male)
14. Most individual Olympic medals (male)
15. Most swimming Olympic medals won, men (single games)

The climate of Africa ranges from [tropical](/wiki/Tropical_climate "Tropical climate") to [subarctic](/wiki/Subarctic_climate "Subarctic climate") on its highest peaks. Its northern half is primarily [desert](/wiki/Desert "Desert"), or [arid](/wiki/Arid "Arid"), while its central and southern areas contain both [savanna](/wiki/Savanna "Savanna") plains and dense [jungle](/wiki/Jungle "Jungle") (rainforest) regions. In between, there is a convergence, where vegetation patterns such as [sahel](/wiki/Sahel "Sahel") and [steppe](/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") dominate. Africa is the hottest continent on Earth and 60% of the entire land surface consists of drylands and deserts.[[160]](#cite_note-environmentalatlas-168) The record for the highest-ever recorded temperature, in [Libya](/wiki/Libya "Libya") in 1922 (58 °C (136 °F)), was discredited in 2013.[[161]](#cite_note-newRecord-169)[[162]](#cite_note-170)
